next_steps: Maya to share tuned quantization config and artifacts (quant-config-v3.zip)
Ethan to schedule 24h stability run on dedicated pool w/ real traffic replay
Lumina to provide 2 additional eval prompt sets for edge cases by 2026-10-11
Schedule roll-forward playbook review with Lumina SREs week of 2026-10-13
action_items: Maya Patel: send quant-config-v3.zip and short notes (due 2026-10-12)
Ethan Torres: prepare 24h load script + runbook (due 2026-10-14)

summary: Weekly POC check-in for Lumina Health low-precision pilot. Reviewed INT8 and FP8 runs against baseline fp16 for both quality and perf. INT8 showed modest 6-8% SNR drop on edge prompts but 1.9x throughput improvement in bursty scenarios; FP8 gave similar perf with slightly better quality but needed kernel stability tuning. Agreed to run a 24h stability replay on dedicated capacity and share tuned quant configs. Security questions around KMS and VPC clarified; next meeting to review runbook and playbook for rollback/canary.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-07 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Ethan Torres, Sofia Martinez (Redwood); Jared Kim, Priya Rao, Tom Nguyen, Asha Mehta, Ben Ortiz (Lumina)
Shared: quant-results-2026-10-07.xlsx (link), quant-config-v3.zip (to follow), replay-traces.tar.gz (link)

[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining the sync, um this is Maya from Redwood, how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Priya Rao: good thanks, busy week but ready to go.
[00:09] Jared Kim: hey Maya, morning. excited to see the numbers.
[00:13] Ethan Torres: quick agenda — run through perf deltas, quality deltas, anomalies from last run, decide next run plan and security check. ok?
[00:20] Tom Nguyen: yep that works. I'm mostly here for the stability/runbook bits.
[00:24] Maya Patel: great. Ethan, you wanna start with throughput/latency?
[00:28] Ethan Torres: sure, so slide up — uh in the sheet we ran three branches: baseline fp16, int8 (dynamic range) and fp8 bfloat-esque blend. Results quick summary: int8 gave roughly 1.8-2.0x increase in tokens/sec on p3/rt-like instances with continuous batching, latency p50 improved by ~30-35% on average but p95 had more variance under burst. fp8 is closer in quality to fp16, perf gains about 1.5x, smoother p95.
[00:57] Jared Kim: can you repeat the p95 comment, we saw p95 spikes on our dev run yesterday.
[01:02] Ethan Torres: yeah so int8's kernel path currently has a couple of edge cases where attention softmax under longer context causes a fallback to slower path — that's why you see p95 spiking when sequence length > 1k or when KV cache warms. we logged those as ticket INF-842 but patching kernel lowers spike but needs validation.
[01:25] Asha Mehta: so for our clinical summaries (which are longer) does that mean int8 might underperform sometimes?
[01:30] Ethan Torres: potentially yes on very long sequences. in most patient-summary cases where average context is ~600 tokens, we saw int8 still wins for throughput. it's the outliers above ~1k that cause the p95 problem.
[01:40] Priya Rao: do you have numbers for quality deltas? we care about hallucination and SNR for decision-critical outputs.
[01:46] Ethan Torres: yes, we ran the eval sets you gave plus a seeded set of edge prompts. int8 showed a 6-8% drop in the primary metric (ROUGE-style surrogate we used) and some increased token-level entropy on ambiguous prompts. fp8 was 1-2% lower than fp16, so much closer. i'll note these are model dependent — some model variants are resilient.
[02:10] Jared Kim: the 6-8% is worrying for prod, especially for clinical. could we do a hybrid? run fp8 for the critical paths and int8 for lighter workloads?
[02:18] Maya Patel: yes that's exactly one of the routing policies we recommend — smart routing by policy: critical routes pinned to fp8 or fp16, lower-risk routes to int8. Redwood supports automatic fallback when quality thresholds are violated too.
[02:32] Ben Ortiz: quick sec, from security side — does quantization affect encryption or KMS keys handling? we had a question — if model artifacts are quantized, are keys rotated differently?
[02:41] Sofia Martinez: good q. quantized weights are still stored and encrypted the same way in Redwood Private. KMS operations are unchanged; it's about artifact management. however for on-prem builds we can integrate with your HSM if needed. we'll send a short note.
[02:56] Ben Ortiz: ok please do, also SOC2 artifact for this pilot.
[03:00] Maya Patel: yes will share SOC2 + SOC2 type ii extract and our security checklist.
[03:04] Ethan Torres: back to perf — one more note, prefix caching / KV cache hit rates matter. If you have many short repeated prefixes we can get dramatic cost savings with int8 since memory bandwidth improves, but if your workload is unique long contexts the benefit shrinks.
[03:20] Tom Nguyen: our workload is mixed — patient intake forms are short, summaries are long. any recommendations for batch sizing?
[03:26] Ethan Torres: start conservative. batch target of 32 with latency SLO 300ms p95 for short queries; for long ones reduce batch to 8 or use dedicated lower-batch lane. autoscaling policies can maintain those lanes. Also prefix cache TTL was tuned to 30s in the test; we can tune to your traffic patterns.
[03:45] Priya Rao: what about cost delta — any ballpark?
[03:48] Maya Patel: based on token-per-dollar we saw int8 reduce token cost by ~45% in the test harness when cache hit was high; fp8 around 30%. real numbers depend on KV hit and batch. we'll give a modeled sheet for Lumina's traffic patterns.
[04:02] Jared Kim: interesting. we ran a short A/B yesterday and saw some generation token-level oddities — sentences repeating in int8 outputs. any known regressions?
[04:12] Ethan Torres: we saw a couple repeating loops on certain rare prompt templates; traced to quantization sensitivity in layernorm scaling in that model. our mitigation was a small calibration pass (per-layer scaling) in quant-config-v3 which reduced repeats by ~80% in our re-runs.
[04:28] Asha Mehta: will that add extra latency?
[04:31] Ethan Torres: negligible at runtime, calibration cost is offline. runtime uses the adjusted kernels; small extra memory but not much latency impact.
[04:38] Priya Rao: good. Security follow-up: for the dedicated pool you mentioned, is that on our VPC? how do we isolate traffic?
[04:45] Maya Patel: yes, Dedicated runs in a customer VPC with optional private link. You get VPC peering or private connect, subnets, and telemetry goes to your logging endpoint — logs can be routed to your SIEM. We also support inbound whitelisting and mTLS.
[04:58] Ben Ortiz: KMS rotation policy?
[05:00] Sofia Martinez: keys rotate per your schedule; Redwood uses envelope encryption; we'll share the KMS integration doc.
[05:06] Ethan Torres: quick anomaly we found — during the int8 nightly run on 10/04 there was a throughput regression tied to a new kernel that mis-handled causal mask in very long sequences, we rolled back to prior kernel. fixes are in staging, need validation.
[05:21] Jared Kim: so is rollback easy? can we automate fallback to fp16 if we detect quality or latency regression?
[05:26] Maya Patel: yes you can set policy-based fallback. we offer canary percentages and automatic fallback when metrics cross thresholds (latency or quality). we recommend a small canary first: 5-10% traffic for int8, watch SLOs, then ramp.
[05:40] Tom Nguyen: what metrics should we monitor in the canary? p95 latency, error rate, prompt-level quality score?
[05:46] Ethan Torres: p95 latency, token generation error rate (exceptions), and a quality sentinel which is a small autoeval on sampled prompts (we can plug your eval set). also monitor model-side memory pressure so GPU OOMs don't slip by.
[06:00] Maya Patel: for the 24h stability run we propose to replay a day's production traffic anonymized, run int8 and fp8 branches with 10% canary on live cluster and measure regressions. Ethan will prepare the replay.
[06:12] Ethan Torres: yes, I'll set up a dedicated pool with the quantized kernels and run the replay — we'll capture p50/p95, throughputs, token-level diffs, and a sample of outputs sent to your eval harness.
[06:24] Priya Rao: timeline?
[06:26] Ethan Torres: if we get prompt sets by 10/11 and we provision the dedicated pool Monday 10/12 we can start the 24h run 10/13 and have postmortem 10/14.
[06:37] Jared Kim: ok. any expected downtime for our prod?
[06:39] Maya Patel: none. this will be on the dedicated pilot cluster and won't affect your prod until you opt in the routing policy.
[06:46] Ben Ortiz: about compliance — can logs be redacted? we need PHI-safe exports for the eval samples.
[06:52] Sofia Martinez: yes, we support redaction hooks and can run evals on pseudonymized traces. we'll provide the recommended pattern.
[06:58] Asha Mehta: on the evaluation side we want the model to preserve key medical entities but not invent new ones — how did you test that?
[07:05] Ethan Torres: we added entity-precision and entity-recall checks to the eval harness. int8 had a small drop in precision on a handful of cases; fp8 retained near-baseline. We'll include a per-entity breakdown in the artifacts.
[07:21] Maya Patel: ok let's cover anomalies from last run — Ethan?
[07:25] Ethan Torres: right — we cataloged three anomalies: 1) p95 spike on long seqs (kernel fallback) 2) repetition loops on a rare prompt family (mitigated by per-layer calibration) 3) an OOM on a transient heavy batch that we've addressed by adjusting batch scheduler. All three have patches or mitigations; we want validation from your replay.
[07:46] Tom Nguyen: that OOM — did it cause any instance reboot?
[07:49] Ethan Torres: no reboots, just a soft fail on the request with retry; we adjusted queue backpressure to avoid head-of-line blocking.
[07:56] Priya Rao: perfect. on the net effect — if we go with hybrid routing what cost delta should we plan for?
[08:02] Maya Patel: in our modeled traffic with 60% short queries and 40% long summaries, a hybrid of fp8 for summaries + int8 for short queries gave ~32% cost savings vs all-fp16 while keeping quality within 1.5% of baseline on key metrics. we'll send the model sheet.
[08:19] Jared Kim: great. one more technical q — does Redwood support mixed-precision at runtime per layer? i.e., selectively keep some layers fp16 and others int8?
[08:27] Ethan Torres: we support mixed-precision strategies in the compilation step — you can pin specific layers to higher precision. it's in the quant-config; quant-config-v3 includes a sample mixed-precision map.
[08:36] Asha Mehta: can you share that map?
[08:38] Maya Patel: yes, will attach in the artifact ZIP.
[08:41] Priya Rao: any licensing or pricing implications if we run dedicated for pilot?
[08:45] Maya Patel: Dedicated is subscription for the pool plus usage. For pilots we often do short-term reserved credits; I'll loop finance and send a pilot pricing worksheet.
[08:54] Ben Ortiz: and support SLA during pilot?
[08:56] Maya Patel: we provide standard pilot support, and can enable a higher support tier during the run for quicker response.
[09:01] Ethan Torres: action items recap — I'll own the 24h run and data capture, Maya will send artifacts and the pricing worksheet, Lumina to supply eval prompts.
[09:09] Jared Kim: sounds good. quick question — if we hit a quality regression mid-canary can we auto-shift traffic?
[09:14] Maya Patel: yes, automatic fallback triggers are supported — threshold-driven. you'd define your metric and threshold.
[09:20] Tom Nguyen: ok let's define thresholds in next doc.
[09:22] Maya Patel: noted. any other blockers?
[09:25] Priya Rao: Ben will review SOC2 bits and Jared will validate eval sets, otherwise none.
[09:31] Ben Ortiz: i'll send a list of security questions.
[09:33] Maya Patel: perfect. we'll aim to have the artifacts in your inbox by 10/12 and start the 24h on 10/13 pending your prompt sets. thanks everyone.
[09:44] Asha Mehta: thanks all.
[09:46] Jared Kim: thanks.
[09:47] (call ends)

Notes: The transcript shows typical speech disfluencies and minor transcription errors (e.g., 'p3/rt-like' may be mis-transcribed, some proper nouns may be off). Artifacts referenced: quant-results-2026-10-07.xlsx, quant-config-v3.zip, replay-traces.tar.gz.
